claims.text: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that, through its Advisor Services segment, Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients, and that management believes Schwab can maintain its competitive position primarily through its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.
On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab's CEO stated that Schwab has built its advisor business around helping independent advisors grow, compete, and succeed.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs, including lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.

Trade press reports (published October 28, 2026) that Schwab's CEO stated Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for RIAs with under $100 million AUM and that Schwab's role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps RIAs support their clients and helps their firms thrive.

Trade press reports (published August 26, 2026) that a Schwab spokesperson stated Schwab, as the largest custodian for advisors, is focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and retail investors and on investing in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow.

The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that the Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.

The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that RIAs and their clients have access to Schwab's broad range of wealth services and that, by functioning as the custodian, Schwab earns revenue associated with the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees, and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab stated it serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.

In its May 14, 2026 investor day deck, Schwab states that Advisor Services is in a position of strength and remains a driving force for Schwab, with $5.2T in client assets, 16K advisory firms, and 3.9M households, and is #1 in RIA custodial assets.
In its May 14, 2026 investor day deck, Schwab states that Schwab Advisor Services provides custody, trading, and the support services of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. to independent investment advisors.

In its May 14, 2026 investor day deck, Schwab states its strategic priority is to be the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone, including growing lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Schwab stated that in Advisor Services it is continuing to enhance its digital experiences across RIA workflows such as move money, account open, and account maintenance while also modernizing tools on its advisor platform.

On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), Schwab stated that in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Schwab stated it is investing in banking and lending for RIAs as the natural provider of those capabilities and that it is just getting started with its banking journey for RIAs.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Schwab stated that in its advisor services business it launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.

The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that, in the Advisor Services arena, Schwab competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Schwab's CEO stated that RIAs from time to time compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses and that wirehouses are doing a better job of leveraging their banking capabilities.
Trade press reports (published October 29, 2026) that Schwab's CEO stated independent advisors are competing against wirehouses that typically have really strong banks attached to their advice.
On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab's CEO stated that Schwab has changed the minimums for long/short strategies and throttled growth to some extent.
Trade press reports (published October 28, 2026) that Schwab stated it limited long-short offerings to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors.

Trade press reports (published October 28, 2026) that Schwab stated it is reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM.

Trade press reports (published August 24, 2026) that a Schwab spokesperson confirmed the asset minimum for client referrals in Schwab Advisor Network has changed from $2 million to $5 million, effective January 5, 2027.
